clue.text: Include fellow member needing salary increase

parts.note: CO is the prefix meaning fellow or joint, as in co-worker
MP is a Member of Parliament
a rise is a pay increase

explanation.surface: A colleague in the club wants a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: CO stands for 'fellow' through the prefix in co-pilot and co-worker. 'Needing' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To comprise is to contain or be made up of, so it can stand for include.

clue.text: Body Rex found inside the thicket

indicators.note: found inside says the king's letter is placed within the word for the thicket

parts.note: a copse is a small thicket of trees
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A dead body is discovered in a thicket, perhaps with a dog called Rex finding it.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex reads as a dog's name, but here it is the Latin for king, abbreviated R as on coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse is a dead body.

clue.text: Hothead gets furious over EU farming policy

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: mad means furious
CAP is the Common Agricultural Policy of the European Union

explanation.surface: An angry farmer rages about Brussels' agricultural subsidies.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is a reckless, impulsive person, much like a hothead.

clue.text: Has memories about everyone in the Civil Service

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the abbreviation for the service

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A retired official reminisces about all his colleagues in Whitehall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Civil Service is the body of British government administrators, abbreviated CS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who recalls things remembers them, so has memories of them.

clue.text: Failing to take a brief approach

definitions.meaning: a failing is a fault or defect
read as two words: a ..., an arrival that is brief

explanation.definitionFit: A shortcoming is a flaw or weakness; split in two it describes a short arrival.

clue.text: Such a type deserves no good fortune

definitions.text: Such a type deserves no good fortune

parts.words: Such a type deserves no good fortune
parts.note: a rogue is described, and also a share of fate (a lot) that is unlucky

explanation.definitionFit: A bad lot is a dishonest person; lot also means one's fortune or destiny, which here is bad.

clue.text: Concoction I need as flavouring

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up from ingredients, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook mixing something up decides they need a flavouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concoction' signals rearranging the seven letters of I NEED AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is the seed of the anise plant, used to flavour sweets and drinks.

clue.text: What a tall man wears to gain advantage?

definitions.meaning: a lengthy suit of clothes, fitting someone tall
in card games a ... is a strong holding, hence a strength or advantage

explanation.definitionFit: A long suit is one's strong point, from holding many cards of one suit at bridge or whist.

clue.text: Go and fish by the tollgate

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'
a pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler heads off fishing near the old toll road.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike was a toll road or the barrier where the toll was paid.

clue.text: Editor backed the German performer

indicators.note: backed says the German article is written backwards

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: An editor supported a German entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' reads as 'supported' in the surface, but here it is the reversal signal on the German article.
explanation.definitionFit: A redactor is one who edits or revises text for publication.

clue.text: Pole enters modest cafe to order it

definitions.text: Pole enters modest cafe to order it

indicators.note: enters says the pole's letter goes into the word for the cafe

parts.note: a diner is a simple, cheap restaurant
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish visitor walks into a cheap restaurant to order a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole reads as a person from Poland; here it is the North Pole, N. The whole clue also describes what you go to a diner for.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is the meal you would walk into a cheap restaurant to order.

clue.text: Small vehicle rented for cardinal

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a car is a vehicle
let means rented out

explanation.surface: A small hire car is laid on for a visiting church cardinal.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal looks like the churchman, but it is the colour of his robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal is a deep red, the colour of a cardinal's vestments.

clue.text: Exercise makes journalists elated

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively
up means in high spirits

explanation.surface: Reporters are delighted after a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor exercise pushing the body up with the arms.

clue.text: Made the boss switch on the electricity

definitions.meaning: read literally, to load up with electrical current

explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in charge is to give them command; read literally it means supplying a current.

clue.text: Saw a detective being sweet

parts.note: to have spotted something is to have seen it
a dick is slang for a private detective

explanation.surface: Someone saw a private eye who was being kind.
explanation.walkthrough: SPOTTED DICK is a British steamed suet pudding with currants; 'sweet' is the British word for dessert, not a kind adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: This traditional currant pudding is a dessert, which British speakers call a sweet.

clue.text: Criminal with allure is held in scorn

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
to tempt is to allure

explanation.surface: A seductive crook is looked down on.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is the feeling of disdain or scorn.

clue.text: Brazen opposition from French husband-to be

parts.note: de is French for from or of
a fiance is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's intended faces open resistance to the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is bold, open resistance.

clue.text: Poor Natalie could be working

indicators.note: could be signals that these letters may be made into something else

explanation.surface: Poor Natalie might be at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like pity for Natalie, but it is part of the eleven letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something operational is functioning or in use.

clue.text: One in mental distress requires sustenance

indicators.note: in says the number one goes inside the rearranged letters
distress suggests a disordered state, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in a mental crisis needs nourishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' turns MENTAL into ALMENT, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is food or nourishment.

clue.text: Many honour poet from northern Italy

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a large number
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A much-decorated poet hails from the north of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving L (Roman fifty) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Lombardy is a region of northern Italy, and Lombard describes its people or things.

clue.text: Remain united once the colonel's present

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, such as a colonel
here means present, as at roll call

explanation.surface: The troops stick together when the colonel turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colonel's' is read as 'colonel is', so the pieces are CO and HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together or hold firm as one.

clue.text: Approved of girl getting absorbed in dictionary

indicators.note: getting absorbed in says the girl's name is placed inside the dictionary's letters

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
Kay is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl engrossed in a dictionary earns approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To have okayed something is to have given it the go-ahead.

clue.text: Removing stalks made team leader sick

indicators.note: the leader of the team is its first letter

parts.note: ailing means sick

explanation.surface: The captain of the side fell ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailing is pulling the stalks off fruit such as gooseberries, as in 'top and tail'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail fruit is to cut off its stalk end, so stripping the stems is this.

clue.text: A couple of males in joint providing sleeping accommodation

indicators.note: in places the pair of males inside the joint

parts.note: the hock is the ankle joint of a horse or other animal

indicators.note: couple of says the letter for male appears twice over

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Two men in a pub find somewhere to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a pub or a cut of meat, but it is the animal's ankle; 'providing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammock is a hanging bed of netting or canvas.

clue.text: The little devil has my French translation

parts.note: mon is French for my
a key is a crib or set of translations for a text

explanation.surface: A naughty child has my French homework crib.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is affectionately called a little monkey, or little devil.

clue.text: Elaborately dressed Tyrolean

indicators.note: dressed suggests the letters are rearranged or arranged in a new way

explanation.surface: Someone from the Tyrol is in fancy costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornately means with elaborate decoration.

clue.text: A number from the regiment went yesterday

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Some soldiers of the regiment left yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across regimenT WENT Yesterday.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is a number, two tens.

clue.text: Late principal used to keep the roses tidy

parts.note: late means dead, as in 'the late king'
a head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: A deceased headmaster once looked after the rose garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners pinch off spent blooms so the plant keeps flowering, which tidies roses.
